summary: Shigeru Kato (1880–1946) worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1903 to 1906 and later held a post there from circa 1925 to 1941.

Shigeru Matsumoto (1933–2010) was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1961) and Harvard University (~1963–1967). He held posts at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1970–1998) and Tenri University.
Shih-Hsiang Chen (1912–1971) was a sinologist who studied at Peking University from circa 1932 to 1936. He served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1945 to 1971.
Shikaripur N. Sridhar works in linguistics and indology. At Stony Brook University, he is attested as Chair in 2007 and as Director of the Center for India Studies in 2026.
Shikazo Mori (1906–1980) specialized in history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929 and held a post at Bukkyo University from circa 1970 to 1980.

Shili Xiong (1885–1968) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology, studying under Jian Ouyang at the China Institute of Inner Learning in 1920. He held posts at Boone University (~1919–1920), Peking University (1923–1955), and Zhejiang University (~1944–1946).

Shimei Futabatei (1864–1909) studied at Senshu College, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Hitotsubashi University. In linguistics and other fields, he held posts at the Army and Naval War Colleges, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and two Asahi Shimbun newspapers.

Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of indology and philosophy. His career includes attested posts at Hiroshima University in 1992 and as Associate Professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College in 2000.

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (1889–1980) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami, earning a doctorate at Kyoto University. He held professorships at Hanazono, Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Kyoto City University of Arts, and visited Harvard in 1958.

Shin'ichi Tsuda (b. 1938) is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Tokyo and ANU under Akira Hirakawa, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later holding posts at Toyo Bunko, Toho Gakuin, and ICPBS.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga (1957–2022) specialized in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University and held a post as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College, attested in 2015.

Shindai Sekiguchi (1907–1986) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1928–1931). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1959–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1983).

Shindo Kusumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Hiroshima University by 2001, studying under Shoryu Katsura, Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shingen Takagi (b. 1932) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Tohoku and Rissho, taught by Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served at Koyasan University as associate professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo (b. 1948) specializes in indology and religious studies. He studied under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (~1974–1980) and held a post at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~1989–2013).
Shingo Enomoto (b. 1948) is an indologist who earned a PhD from the University of Marburg (~1974–1980). From circa 1982 to 1989, he held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology.

Shinichi Nakazawa (b. 1950) works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1970–1977), he held posts at Chuo University (~1993–2002), Tama Art University (~2006), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinjiro Kazama (b. 1965) is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University from circa 1984 to 1994. He held a post at Tottori University (~1996–2004) and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2004.

Shinjo Mochizuki (1899–1990) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (~1922–1925), and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.

Shinjo Suguro (1925–2002) studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948, doctorate 1987). He was vice director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and professor at Rissho University (~1965–1996, emeritus ~1996–2002).
